goal.objective:
`data/chain.txt` starts with a line `NEXT=<file>`. Follow that link (files live in
`data/`; `<file>` is the exact file name, e.g. `p01.txt`). Each linked file also
starts with `NEXT=<file>` and `N=<integer>` (e.g. `N=11`; the number is the text
after the `N=` prefix).

Keep following `NEXT` until it says `NEXT=END`, summing every `N` value you pass.
After each file, write the next file name (or `END`) into `src/position.txt` and
keep `src/running-total.txt` holding the sum of the N values you have visited so
far. If your context is compacted, read those two files first to recover your
place instead of re-reading files you already visited.
Write the total (as decimal digits) plus a single trailing newline into
`src/answer.txt`.

Work through the chain with the file-reading tool (do not delegate the traversal
to a shell loop), and write the answer with the file-writing tool.

Change nothing else.

fresh_install.detail: Downloaded leveler-v1.0.25-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz from the public release; sha256 matched the published .sha256 (5c867653…90ca). Extracted into a clean directory and ran with an empty LEVELER_HOME: `--version` reports 1.0.25 (3a3fa8fb7702). `doctor` passes every host check; only the expected 'no providers/models configured' lines fail in an empty HOME.

upgrade.detail: Created a fresh state store with v1.0.24 (its head migration is 51), then started v1.0.25 on the same LEVELER_HOME and repo: the runtime became ready and migrated the store to head 52 (session recaps). No migration error, no data reset. Downgrade is refused by design: v1.0.24 on a schema-52 store fails closed.

soak.headline: 24-hour Soak: FAIL — Reliability Certification Failed
soak.note: 12,118 runs: 11,367 succeeded, 3 failed, 746 skipped (policy), 2 unknown (injected fault). The 3 failures were scheduled shell runs on 2026-11-11T00:45:20Z (os-tick, os-pause, misfire-runonce) that could not get a session snapshot within 30 s while the host showed a CPU spike (sample 67.9%); the runtime logs from that window are gone, so the cause (runtime stall vs host starvation) is not proven. S4_2 / S4_allow_execution_2 failed on a 180 s observation window, but the overlap store shows queue-one occurrences running back-to-back throughout the run, so that check is a probe-timing gap, not a policy failure. RSS max 494 MB, under the 512 MiB growth threshold. The 24-hour reliability certification is FAILED and is not rewritten as PASS.

conditional_release.reason: The release was published under a waiver limited to the soak's remaining duration. That soak has now completed 24 hours and returned FAIL (3/12,118 runs hit a 30 s runtime-snapshot timeout under a load spike; a further probe-timing check failed). The waiver therefore no longer applies to a pending run: the final reliability certification is FAILED, while every functional gate (L0-L4, RC, three-platform CI) passed and the artifacts are verified.
conditional_release.risk: A transient 30 s runtime unresponsiveness under heavy local load affected 3 scheduled shell runs (0.025%), with no duplicate side effects, stranded occurrences or unsettled runs. The runtime recovered and the run completed. It is a reliability signal for long-running, loaded hosts; the exact cause is unproven because the runtime logs from the 00:45Z window were not preserved.
conditional_release.rollback: No data-integrity failure was observed, so an emergency rollback is not indicated by this evidence. The honest options are: (a) assess and fix the runtime-unresponsive path and ship a forward hotfix (v1.0.26) with its own gates, (b) keep v1.0.25 published with this failed certification clearly labeled, or (c) withdraw the release. A v1.0.24 downgrade cannot open a schema-52 store; restore a pre-upgrade backup instead. The choice needs the user's decision.

known_issues: Downgrading a schema-52 store to v1.0.24 is refused by design; rollback is a forward patch or a pre-upgrade backup.

Feature coverage ends at CONDITIONAL PASS: 2 features unverified (session replay corpus without a corpus; TUI slash fork), 51 declared gaps, performance collected but not compared against a hard threshold (perf hard-fail disabled in this phase).

The Linux x86_64 archive is built on Ubuntu 24.04 and requires glibc >= 2.39 (v1.0.24 has the same floor). It runs on Ubuntu 24.04+, Fedora 40+ and Debian 13+, but not on Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. The CI matrix still tests the source on ubuntu-22.04; the archive's glibc floor is a build-image choice in release.yml, not a code regression in this release.
